t.1.223.1: The wise man stays watchful before a time of hardship arrives; when the time of hardship comes upon him, he never suffers distress at all.
t.1.223.2: But the thoughtless one who does not perceive a calamity before it has arrived is distressed when the time of calamity comes and knows nothing at all.
t.1.223.3: You are steadfast and wise, and this is a peril to our lives. For among many, only one is truly brave and wise; there is no doubt of that.
t.1.223.4: The eldest is indeed the protector; the eldest releases us from distress. If the eldest does not know the way, what will the younger do?
t.1.223.6: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by his brothers, Jaritāri, with joined palms, praised Vibhāvasu; hear, O king, how he did so.
t.1.223.5: Hiraṇyaretas, blazing, comes swiftly toward our dwelling. The seven-tongued Fire, hungry, creeps closer, licking all around.
t.1.223.8: Upward and downward they go, and they spread out from the sides, your flames, O one of great valor, like the rays of the sun.
t.1.223.7: You are the self of Vāyu, the purifier, and the body of the plants; the waters are your womb, O Śukra, and you are the womb of the waters.
t.1.223.10: O Agni, by that auspicious form of yours and by those seven flames that are yours, protect us today, praised as you are by one who seeks refuge.
t.1.223.9: Our mother has gone away, and we do not know our father; our wings have not yet grown, O Abjaketu. We have no protector other than you, O Agni; therefore protect us, O peerless hero.
t.1.223.12: O Agni, you alone are everything; in you rests this whole world. You sustain all beings, and you uphold the world.
t.1.223.11: You alone, O Jātavedas, exist for burning; no other burner is found among the rays, O god. Protect us, who are young seers; pass on beyond us, O Havyavāha.
t.1.223.13: You are Agni, you are the bearer of oblations, and you yourself are the supreme oblation. The wise worship you in many forms and also as one alone.
t.1.223.14: Having created these three worlds, O Havyavāha, when the appointed time has come you cook them again, blazing forth. You alone, O Agni, are the source of this whole universe, and you are again its resting place.
t.1.223.15: O lord of the world, dwelling within living beings, you, ever increasing, digest the food they have eaten; in you everything is established.
t.1.223.16: Becoming the sun, O Jātavedas, you take up with your rays the water of the earth and all the juices born of the earth, and then, at the time of release, you pour them forth and with rain make all things here flourish, O Śukra.
t.1.223.17: From you, O Śukra, these plants with green leaves are born again, and the lotus ponds, and the ocean, the great reservoir of waters.
t.1.223.18: This indeed is the abode, the final refuge of Varuṇa, O sharp-rayed one. Be our gracious protector; do not destroy us today.
t.1.223.19: O tawny-eyed one, red-necked one, you whose path is black, eater of oblations, pass by far away from us and spare us, as you spare the dwellings of the ocean.
t.1.223.22: For you were entrusted to me earlier by Mandapāla, who said, "While burning the forest, you should spare my little sons."
t.1.223.21: You are indeed the seer Droṇa, for what you have spoken is brahman. I shall do what you desire, and you have nothing to fear.
t.1.223.20: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Droṇa of unwearied deeds, Jātavedas, gladdened in spirit and bound by his promise to Mandapāla, spoke to Droṇa.
t.1.223.25: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The Fire did just so; having granted leave to the Śārṅgakas, he blazed up and burned the Khāṇḍava forest, O Janamejaya.
t.1.223.23: That word of his, and what you have spoken here, both of these weigh heavily with me; tell me, what shall I do for you? I am greatly pleased by your hymn of praise, O brahman, O mighty one; blessings be upon you.
t.1.223.24: These little cats constantly torment us, O Śukra; take them, together with their kin, between your fangs, O Havyavāha.
